history.summary: Koubru Laikha is one of the better-known Shiva temples of Manipur, on the bank of the Imphal River at Phoibih along NH-39 (Imphal-Dimapur highway), Saitu Gamphazol area. It is associated with Mount Koubru (Kabru), one of Manipur's highest peaks; local belief holds that milk offered on Koubru mountain flows to this temple, and that the Pandavas visited the mountain. It draws large crowds at Shivaratri and Kanwad. An AGAM Online TV video records an inauguration function at 'Kabru Leikha Mandir' on 17/10/2020, suggesting the present mandir structure is recent. CSV town 'Senapati' is wrong - correct locality is Phoibih / Saitu Gamphazol in Kangpokpi district (verify).

name: Koubru Laikha Temple
town_description: Phoibih is a settlement on NH-39 (the Imphal-Dimapur highway) in the Saitu Gamphazol area of Kangpokpi district, north of Imphal, on the bank of the Imphal River near Mount Koubru. The surrounding Senapati-Kangpokpi hill belt is known for the Dzukou Valley, Purul's traditional games, and the Laonii rice-transplanting festival of the Poumai Nagas. Phoibih lies on the main highway corridor linking Manipur to Nagaland.

travel.railway: No railway station in the district; nearest railheads are Dimapur (Nagaland) and Silchar (Assam), 100+ km away (verify)
travel.road: Directly on NH-39 (Imphal-Dimapur highway) at Phoibih, ~30 km south of Senapati town (verify)
